name: Build a Tree
description: You are given two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$. Construct a tree$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices such that $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n} \operatorname{dist}(i, (i \bmod n) + 1) = k$$$$$$^{\text{†}}$$$, or determine that no such tree exists. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$$$$\operatorname{dist}(i, j)$$$ is the number of edges on the shortest path from vertex $$$i$$$ to vertex $$$j$$$ in the tree.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The only line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$0 \le k \le n^2$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree and the required value of $$$k$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, if there is no solution, output $$$-1$$$. Otherwise, output $$$n - 1$$$ lines. Each line should contain two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$), denoting an edge of the tree. The edges may be output in any order. If there are multiple suitable trees, output any of them.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.
